chapter: Michael, influences and the Brecker Brothers
title: James Brown, Philly R&B radio and Cameo Parkway
summary: As a boy he found James Brown and Stevie Wonder on AM radio after bebop on WHAT; Philly's soul jazz and Cameo Parkway dance records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Would that include James Brown? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Oh sure, sure. I had listened to him as a kid you know, going back to when I was still home in Philly the R&B station — it’s unusual — most guys will say that they listened to rock & roll or R&B first and then they caught on to jazz. I did the opposite. I hadn’t heard all this other stuff, I was just hearing bebop at home. And one day, and I’d always listened to the radio, the jazz station, WHAT, before I went to sleep but there was another station on the AM dial that was right past the jazz station. I think the AM jazz station was WHAT that was the FM station. But all of a sudden I’m probably 10 or 11 or 12 years old and I heard James Brown and Little Stevie Wonder and all that stuff for the first time and that had a — you know I probably sat up straight in bed. That just hit a nerve. And like I mentioned there was a lot of that style of music around in Philly with that kind of influenced stuff, organ trios, soul jazz, and all the records that came out of Philly they were kind of like Motown. The label that I started talking about was Cameo Parkway. And they were all founded, it was founded by jazz musicians, a guy named Dave Appell was one of the guys who had written charts I think for Jimmie Lunceford, and all these guys I mentioned before there was a — and it was similar to Motown. They’d invent dances, you know it wasn’t just coincidence there were so many dances coming out of Philly — the Mashed Potato and the Twist and the Bunny Hop. So in a way looking back on it it was kind of amazing. So there was just a big influence. But by the time I got to New York that was just the style to burn. “Come on man, we’re going to bash.” And then things kind of as we aged I think now everyone knows how to hold back a little.
